method: N concurrent single-transaction publishers against one Log; OFF = one durability barrier per publish, ON = one barrier per batch (bounded by max count and max wait)
note: the win comes only from fewer fsync barriers, so it tracks the backing store's fsync cost; a batch of up to 64 transactions shares one barrier. On this backing an uncontended single publish (encode+append+one fsync) costs 17943 ns, so the win is bounded by both the barrier cost and the per-batch CPU to frame/append the batch. Measured throughput_on/throughput_off=4.31x, p50_off/p50_on=4.49x. The OFF arm is the honest baseline: without group commit, concurrent publishes serialize and each pays its own fsync. Run inside the court container (overlay/ext4) where fsync has real cost; on tmpfs the win is expected to be small or absent.
